title: Kam AI: Private Offline AI
shortDescription: Thinks with you, not for you. Private AI on your phone, with no account.
fullDescription:
Kam AI runs on your phone. Download a model once, and after that everything happens on the device: what you ask, what it answers, and anything you save. Nothing is uploaded. Put the phone in airplane mode and you can still chat.

It thinks with you, not for you. That is what the four modes are for, and it is why one of them will not hand you ideas at all.

THE FOUR MODES

Logic Partner takes the other side. Describe a plan or an argument and it looks for what is weak in it, asks the question you have been avoiding, and says where the reasoning does not hold. It concedes when you are right, and it does not fold just because you pushed back. Most assistants agree with you by default. This one is built not to.

Brainstorm pulls your own ideas out of you, one question at a time, instead of handing you a list.

Workbench takes text you paste in and tightens, rewrites or reorganizes it. The before and the after stay side by side.

General handles everything else.

ALSO INSIDE

Voice, so you can talk instead of typing, transcribed on the phone.
Projects, which keep related chats under instructions and notes they all share.
Memory of the durable things, all of it visible and deletable.
Bookmarks for anything worth coming back to, and search across your chats, projects and bookmarks.
Discover, offline packs of short readings to pull one from and talk about.

WHAT TO EXPECT

Answers take a few seconds. The first one after installing takes longest while the model loads, and it is slower again when the phone is warm. That wait is your phone doing work a data center would otherwise do with your words, which is the same reason nothing you type leaves the device.

A model small enough to fit on a phone knows less than the large ones in data centers, and it guesses more, so it will get obscure facts wrong. Anything factual is worth checking, which is what the bookmarks are for. It cannot make images. Without a connection it knows nothing about recent events. And it is better at working with text you give it than at writing long polished documents from nothing.

Logic Partner and Brainstorm ask more of the model than General and Workbench do, because holding an argument or running a session means keeping track of what you said several turns ago, and a smaller model does that less reliably. If those modes are why you are here and your phone has the room, the larger model is worth the space. The app measures speed on your own phone, recommends a size, and says plainly where a smaller one is weaker.

WHAT IT ASKS YOUR PHONE FOR

The internet, only to download a model, a voice or a content pack when you choose to, and to check what packs are available when you open Discover.
Whether you have a connection and whether it is metered, so a multi-gigabyte download never starts on mobile data without you saying so.
A notification while a download is running, so it can carry on when you leave the app.
The microphone, only when you use voice typing, which is transcribed on the phone.
Your fingerprint or face, only if you turn on the app lock.

That is the whole list. No account, no ads, no tracking, and nothing to subscribe to.

Free and open source, under the AGPLv3.
